new_symbol_range_suggestions.subleading_logarithmic_running_amplitude: nonnegative and typically modest, with 1 + subleading_logarithmic_running_amplitude * log(1 + (L / subleading_running_crossover_size)**subleading_running_sharpness) staying positive over sampled L; often 0 to order-unity
new_symbol_range_suggestions.subleading_running_crossover_size: positive, typically comparable to intermediate sampled system sizes if the onset of subleading logarithmic running is to be observable
new_symbol_range_suggestions.subleading_running_sharpness: positive, order-unity to a few for gradual but finite crossover into the running regime

derivation_notes: The parent assumed the extra subleading correction had a fixed scaling dimension and only a saturating amplitude renormalization. Here that assumption is relaxed by allowing marginal operator mixing to generate a multiplicative logarithmic running factor on the subleading correction itself, implemented with a finite-crossover logarithm so the effect turns on gradually and reduces continuously to the parent when the new running amplitude vanishes.
change_summary: The subleading correction is no longer a pure power law with only denominator suppression; it now acquires an additional multiplicative logarithmic running factor. This changes the asymptotic approach of chi(L) by bending the effective log-log slope over intermediate-to-large sizes where the subleading sector is still visible.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The additional subleading correction-to-scaling contribution is a pure power law in L apart from a saturating amplitude factor, with no logarithmic running in its own scaling dimension.
assumption_audit.mechanism: A marginal or near-marginal irrelevant operator can mix with a subleading irrelevant scaling field, causing the subleading susceptibility correction to acquire multiplicative logarithmic renormalization and hence a slowly varying effective decay exponent.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Set subleading_logarithmic_running_amplitude = 0 to recover the parent expression exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed critical temperature, chi(L) is modeled as a pure sum of power-law finite-size terms with logarithmically renormalized amplitudes, so all nonanalytic size dependence is forced into amplitudes while the effective correction exponents remain fixed.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same critical leading sector but relax the assumption that the additional analytic/irrelevant correction is a pure power with fixed exponent; instead allow the subleading correction itself to acquire multiplicative logarithmic running, changing how its local slope versus log L bends across intermediate and large sizes.
response_change.observable_effect: Across increasing L, the subleading tail shows a slower crossover in effective exponent than any fixed-exponent parent term can mimic with one shared parameter set, producing a distinct drift in d log chi / d log L at sizes where the correction is still visible but the leading term already dominates.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when L is large enough that log(1 + (L / subleading_crossover_size)**subleading_saturation_sharpness) is O(1) or larger, yet not so large that the subleading correction is numerically negligible compared with the leading critical term; this is the intermediate-to-large finite-size regime near the crossover into marginal running.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: The same L-only mechanism already affects the visible training sizes through gradual curvature in effective slopes, and extends in holdout to a stronger long-scale drift rather than introducing a new branch or unsampled condition.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the new logarithmic-running amplitude on the subleading sector is set to zero, or when the associated logarithmic strength tends to zero so the correction reverts to a fixed pure power contribution.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: marginal logarithmic renormalization of a subleading irrelevant correction
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: A marginal or near-marginal irrelevant operator can mix with a subleading irrelevant scaling field, causing the subleading susceptibility correction to acquire multiplicative logarithmic renormalization and hence a slowly varying effective decay exponent.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The refinement does more than rescale a coefficient: it introduces a gradual size-activated logarithmic modulation of the subleading decay law itself, so the effective slope changes with scale in a way a fixed set of power exponents and amplitude renormalizations cannot globally match.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The additional subleading correction-to-scaling contribution is a pure power law in L apart from a saturating amplitude factor, with no logarithmic running in its own scaling dimension.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The subleading correction can mix with a marginal or near-marginal operator and therefore picks up a finite-crossover multiplicative logarithmic running factor.

evolution_contract.after_fragment: (susceptibility_amplitude * (1 + leading_logarithmic_amplitude / (1 + leading_logarithmic_strength * log(1 + (L / leading_logarithmic_crossover_size)**leading_logarithmic_sharpness)))) * L**critical_exponent_ratio + correction_amplitude * L**(critical_exponent_ratio - correction_exponent) + (subleading_correction_amplitude / (1 + logarithmic_correction_strength * log(1 + (L / subleading_crossover_size)**subleading_saturation_sharpness))) * L**(critical_exponent_ratio - subleading_correction_exponent) / (1 + subleading_logarithmic_running_amplitude * log(1 + (L / subleading_running_crossover_size)**subleading_running_sharpness))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set subleading_logarithmic_running_amplitude = 0 to recover the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Vary L while holding the critical temperature, geometry, boundary conditions, and microscopic couplings fixed. The parent target mapping approaches its asymptotic slope through fixed-power correction sectors with only amplitude running, whereas the child shows an additional slow bending of the local log-log slope once L passes the subleading running crossover and before the whole subleading term becomes negligible. This changed target mapping is observable in chi(L) itself, not only in an auxiliary decomposition, as a more persistent intermediate-to-large-L drift in d log chi / d log L.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of all parent parameters cannot generally reproduce this contrast across the same admissible L range because the parent only combines fixed exponents with amplitude renormalizations already specified by its two logarithmic denominators. That structure can shift crossover scales and amplitudes, but it cannot create the extra multiplicative logarithmic suppression of the subleading power that changes the correction's effective exponent continuously over scale. Matching the small-to-intermediate-L curvature would then mis-match the larger-L tail, or vice versa, when one shared parameter set is required.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the extra subleading finite-size correction has a fixed algebraic exponent with only a simple denominator suppression, omitting the realistic case that a marginally irrelevant field can renormalize that correction multiplicatively and therefore alter its effective exponent drift with size.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The additional subleading correction-to-scaling contribution is a pure power law in L apart from a saturating amplitude factor, with no logarithmic running in its own scaling dimension.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: A marginal or near-marginal irrelevant operator can mix with a subleading irrelevant scaling field, causing the subleading susceptibility correction to acquire multiplicative logarithmic renormalization and hence a slowly varying effective decay exponent.
evolution_plan.rationale: Vary L while holding the bath temperature at the critical point, geometry, boundary conditions, and microscopic couplings fixed. The parent mapping gives one leading critical growth law plus fixed-exponent corrections whose amplitudes run slowly. That means once parameters are globally fit, the local log-log slope can only approach the asymptote through the specific combination of fixed powers already present. A natural refinement is to relax the idealization that the subleading correction's exponent is fixed: in marginal cases, operator mixing makes that correction decay with an extra logarithmic factor, changing curvature in the target mapping chi(L), not merely an auxiliary quantity. The contrast is observable when the subleading term is still measurable and its logarithmic running has turned on, producing a slower, scale-dependent approach than a single shared parent parameter set can reproduce across small-to-intermediate and larger L simultaneously. This stays within the same zero-field equilibrium critical scenario, preserves positivity/finite-size finiteness when parameters are chosen admissibly, and has a clear parent-recovery limit if the added marginal running is switched off.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: A finite equilibrium system is tuned to the critical temperature of a continuous thermal phase transition. Systems of different linear sizes are sampled while geometry, boundary conditions, and microscopic couplings are fixed. The target is the zero-field susceptibility inferred from equilibrium order-parameter fluctuations. Scale-free collective correlations make the susceptibility grow with system size according to a critical power.
